utterances.text: [Interpretation] I make note, Mr. President, of that. Thank you very much for that. I was just being very attentive and careful for the benefit of the parties and the Chamber, and I think that the terms that I used were precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is not a debating club, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. This is a court of law. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, are you able to locate on the map the site of the second mortar impact which occurred on the same day?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place a cross with the blue marker on that site, and alongside it, write 2.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to that investigation, were you also assisted by a ballistic expert?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the established direction of fire; in other words, from what area?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: I know, as far as I can recall, that it was the same direction as from Nedzarici. I wrote it down in my report, and I believe that it reflects what the ballistics expert had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you about another incident that you investigated. Did you investigate an incident which occurred on the 20th of July, 1993 involving the shooting of a girl in her home?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: I investigated a murder of a girl in her house, but I don't think that it was on the 20th, but on the 28th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies. Whereabouts did that shooting take place? I withdraw that. When you say "murder," was it murder involving shooting or some other cause?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, shooting from fire weapons. I remember the case very well. It was quite special. Me and two other colleagues, ballistics experts, visited the scene upon a call of a neighbour, who told us that there was shooting going on coming from the Serb positions. If we are talking about the same case, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague is telling me that Mr. Ierace was not precise in terms of the date. What year are we talking about? The date is 28th of July, but we didn't hear the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And Mr. Kucanin, you have said that your recollection is that it was the 28th of July. Is that the 28th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the name of the victim?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: It was a 2-year-old girl whose name was Elma Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was she at the time that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: She was at her home. She was sleeping on a couch with her twin sister, just beneath the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you remembered the case because it was quite special, and when you attended the scene upon the call of the neighbour, the neighbour told you that there was shooting going on coming from the Serb positions. What was the address or at least the location of the place where the victim was sleeping?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: The location was Kosevo Brdo. Whether it was in Jukiceva Street or somewhere else, I can't recall, but it was in the neighbourhood called Kosevsko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please find that neighbourhood on the map and point to it.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: This is the area in question, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please take the blue marker. Are you able to see the street where she lived from the map?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't indicate the street, but it was in this area here, the one that I'm indicating now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place a circle around the area of the street.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you place a number 3 alongside the circle.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. What part of the little girl was hit by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Her head. Her forehead, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the bullet remain in her body or did it pass through her body?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: The bullet passed through her head and remained stuck in the couch where the girl was sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it that it was a fatal wound.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you recover the bullet?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We pulled it out. And the experts were able to establish that it came from a 7.9-calibre weapon. It had a steel jacket which is used for snipers and semi-automatic rifles, so that would be most probably the type of weapon that was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you establish the time, approximately, that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: At this point I cannot recall. If I made a report, I think that that should be in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in order that the witness may refresh his memory, I ask that he be shown a document. For the benefit of my learned colleagues, it's a report which is attached to the statement of this witness dated the 21st of February, 1996. They should a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no objection, so therefore, proceed, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Usher -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sorry for this intervention. Is my learned colleague referring to the statement or the interview concerning additional information? I only have an interview of the 12th of February, but it is not in a form of statement, but in the form of a note.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm referring to a statement which is -- I'm sorry. I'm referring to a report which is attached to that statement. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm listening to the French interpretation. I heard 29th of January -- no, February. I'm sorry. And now I see 21st. Are we talking about the 21st or the 29th of the month?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript and so that it may assist my friends, my learned colleagues, the relevant ERN number for the report in Bosnian is 00269430. I'm happy to provide a copy to my friends to save time from them finding their own copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be helpful, Ms. Pilipovic? We could do it anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me while I obtain another copy for the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, do you recognise the document that you now have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that a report made by you on the 29th of July, 1993 in relation to this incident?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: First of all, in relation to the date of the incident, are you able to refresh your memory from this document as to when it occurred?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to be absolutely sure that we are talking about the same ERN number. Is the number 00269430?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the moment, I don't have a B/C/S version in front of me. Perhaps the witness could place it on the ERN [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the number that I see on the paper is not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that there are two numbers, and the number in the right top corner of the document is the same as you just mentioned, I think, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Let me just check all the figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's because on the English statement we have only one figure, and there seems to be two numbers. In order to avoid confusion, Mr. President, I would like to know what is the right one, what document we are talking about, for the record, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I now have a B/C/S copy, and it does have two numbers, and the number that I first gave is the one that appears on the top right, and that's the number which appears on the screen. The number at the bottom, if that assists my friend, is 00378636. That's the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So this has been clarified. You may proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, on what date was this girl shot?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: You're quite right. I apologise for the confusion. In order for everyone to understand the events, let me try to clarify. At the outset, I indicate that it was a specific event. I remember that the citizens of this neighbourhood complained that there was fire from a nearby Serb house. On that day, several bullets reached this neighbourhood, the Jukiceva Street, and we went to the scene in order to establish where fire was indeed opened from that house. We didn't search the house. We only visually inspected the area and tried to establish the direction from which the fire was opened on that neighbourhood. On that occasion, because we had the report of the killing of the girl, we conducted the investigation on the spot, where the girl was killed. She was killed on the 27th, and the investigation was conducted on the 28th, as you were able to see from the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At what time, approximately, was she shot?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: In the evening, the time indicated in the report is 2200, and I remember that that is what we were told, that it had happened in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries as to whether there was any light source in the room where the girl was lying at the time she was shot?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: No, I did not, although I don't think that that would have affected the activity by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, because there was no rule when fire was opened on civilian targets, whether there was light or not, whether the window was open or shut. It was all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to establish, as a result of your investigation, the source of the fire?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes. Since no one touched the bullet before we arrived, and it was stuck deep into the couch, it pierced the part where you lie on, it ended up in the solid surface, wooden part of the couch. So we had part of the trajectory through the couch, and with the assistance of the mother, who indicated the exact spot where the little girl was sleeping, the ballistics experts made an analysis by inserting a special instrument there, and the trajectory, that part of the path was quite deep, and we were able to tell those people that there was an enemy indeed -- that there was not an enemy in that neighbourhood, that the bullet had come from further away. So we were able to reassure the local citizens that it was not the nearby house that was the firing position but that the firing position was another area of the town which is called Kromolj, and we knew that there was constant fire coming from that position, and the target was this neighbourhood of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the Court usher, could you please look again at the map and identify, if you can, the area of Kromolj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps first ask another question. On line 53, page 53, line -- could you please leave it on the ELMO for second -- the witness testified that she was killed on the 27th, and the investigation was conducted on the 28th, as you were able to see from the report. Of course, we have not seen the report. Could the witness please indicate in the report where the date of the 27th is, because I see 20 of the 7th month, which is, of course, not the same as the 27th. But in relation to his reference to the 28th, would that be the 20th of August? It's unclear to me. Could you please clarify this, at least to see whether the witness could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. I had not noticed that. I thought the witness gave a different answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, would you please look again at your report and could you tell us, by refreshing your memory from your report, the date on which the girl was shot.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: On the 20th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now would you please look at the map and see if you can identify the area from which you say the shot came, namely, Kromolj.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: It's this neighbourhood here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you place a circle around that neighbourhood as it appears on the map, and alongside it, would you please write "3A."

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. On what side of the confrontation line was the area within the circle on the 20th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: On the side controlled by the army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, earlier you said that you did not make any inquiries as to whether there was a light on in the room, and you went on to say why you did not do that. Did you make any conclusion -- I withdraw that. Did you notice whether any other rounds had hit the area, apparently about the same time?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, I did say in the beginning that the locals came to the police station to tell us that there was intensive fire opened on that particular neighbourhood over the last few days, and that was why we had come out. They had established that it was coming from that Serb house, and we went out to the scene to see where it was coming. So there was intensive, frequent fire during several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you conclude that the girl was deliberately shot, or rather, that she was the victim of random fire on the area?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: In my view, it was the latter, and that is, it was simply fire opened randomly at a civilian locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any military activity in the area where she was shot? As a result of your investigations, were you able to discover that?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: No, no, not in this part. I don't know. No. I'd say it was a purely civilian neighbourhood which was far, far away from the demarcation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you were a criminal investigator throughout the period of the armed conflict in Sarajevo and that your investigations were exclusively of civilian areas on the Bosnian government side of the confrontation lines. From September 1992 until August of 1994, approximately how many shelling incidents did you investigate, that is, where civilians were killed as a result of artillery shells or mortar shells landing in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: At that time that you mention, several inspectors conducted investigations. I may have performed up to 20 investigations, I mean, of incidents where civilians were casualties, and I mean those incidents where there were fatalities, where people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During that same period, approximately how many incidents did you investigate where civilians were shot as a result of bullets, were killed as a result of bullets?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: All the investigations that I performed involving civilians -- oh, you mean just bullet wounds or all together, the percentage of that as against those hit by shells and such-like?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll re-ask the question. During that period of September 1992 until August 1994, approximately how many incidents did you investigate personally where civilians were shot?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, it could be -- I wouldn't say half of them, but 30 per cent of them were hit from -- by projectiles from firearms, in my cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to give us an approximate number of such incidents in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: You mean my cases, firearm incident killing civilians --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: -- which I investigated?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, say eight, for instance, eight investigations. I'm giving you an arbitrary figure now, but it can all be documented. Had I known that I'd be asked this, I would have provided the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Did you investigate shootings where there were no fatalities, such as shootings on trams?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how many investigations did you carry out where trams were shot in that same period, that is, from September 1992 until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, I could give you an approximate figure, but I cannot exactly when [sic] I did what, when each of these incidents happened. But there were, I think, three occasions where trams were fired at, but I couldn't give you the exact details right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And do you mean three trams -- three occasions where trams were fired at in that particular period of time?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: That's right, in that particular period of time that you are mentioning, September 1992, August 1994, even though, let me say, there were other teams which were much more involved in this than I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, over the entire period of the armed conflict, from April 1992 until Dayton, towards the end of 1995, how many investigations in total did you carry out in that period where civilians had been casualties of shelling or shooting?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, according to my record, approximately -- well, as regards the sniping or shelling of the city of Sarajevo, I performed more than a hundred investigations, and in all of them, casualties were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, as a result of your investigations, did you develop knowledge of the sources of sniping fire, that is, the places from which civilians in Sarajevo were shot or shot at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I am reading that we are talking about the end of 1995, in line 58. I do not think -- I do not think that that question may be allowed, because I do not think -- because I think it is outside the time frame of the indictment, and I do not think that the question can be allowed in this context, that is, up to the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you please explain the relevance of including in your question also a time which is not included in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that will become clear with the next two questions, if I could be permitted that latitude. Essentially, the next few questions go to whether there was any variation in those sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll repeat that last question. As a result of your investigations, did you develop knowledge of the sources of sniping fire, that is, the places from which civilians in Sarajevo were shot or shot at?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any difference in those places between April and September 1992 compared with September 1992 through to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, no. All those places were active throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the investigations that you carried out where civilians became casualties of shelling, similarly, did you develop knowledge of the sources of fire?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: I did, yes, on the basis of ballistic analysis or in situ, yes, we acquired that type of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that when you attended the investigations, indeed, when you carried out the investigations of the incidents that took place, shelling incidents which took place on the 9th of November, 1993, you were accompanied by a ballistics expert. Whenever you attended the investigation of a shelling incident, did you typically have a ballistic expert with you?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That was mandatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the sources of fire, was there any significant change from the period April to September 1992 compared to September 1992 through to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, no, not really, because from those certain areas it happened, at least through the reports you see, that one area comes up and up again all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So if I could put it this way, did some areas or places become notorious for sniper fire or shelling?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From time to time, did you discuss the sources of fire with your fellow investigators?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many other investigators were there operating between September 1992 and August 1994 carrying out the same type of investigations as yourself?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, 20 inspectors maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result of their investigations, as you understood it, was there any degree of agreement between you as a group as to the notorious sources of sniping fire and shelling?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Last week did you mark on a map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I just interrupt you? The objection raised earlier by Mr. Piletta-Zanin was that your question included the period of August 1994 up until December 1995, and you told us that you would ask the witness to compare the periods later on. I heard you asking now a comparison between the period of April until September 1992 and then from 1992 up until August 1994, but I think the objection was that you will -- you included in the number you asked for the period of August 1994 until, well, let's say December 1995. So if all the investigations would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have specifically been in that period, of course the comparison is not complete. You have compared for the earlier period but not with the later period. And I think it was about the later period that the objection of Mr. Piletta-Zanin was referring to. So since I allowed you to proceed, I think it's fair that you complete your comparison in all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you conducted in excess of 100 investigations throughout the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how many of those investigations did you conduct from August 1994 through to the end of the armed conflict in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Well, I'd say majority, an overwhelming majority could be 80 per cent of all the cases I performed between August 1994 and the end of the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any difference in the sources of fire, that is, for sniping and shelling, in that latter period compared to the period September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: No. Same areas came up over and over again, these areas from which sniper fire was opened, as we called them, the sniping areas, and the areas that were hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, last week, did you place some marks on a map of Sarajevo indicating those notorious sources of sniping and shelling fire?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown P36 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. President, thank you for giving me the floor. I note that this map which is to be shown has to relate to 80 per cent, to 80 per cent of incidents which have nothing to do with General Galic, because this is the elements which happened after August 1994. And if it is that map which was premarked, that is a map -- then this is a map which the Defence cannot accept as such, including what the witness -- bearing in mind what the witness has just said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Mr. Ierace, the Chamber is of the opinion that we need at least a clear indication right at the beginning of the questioning in relation to this marked map, whether there are incidents marked and to what extent that happened after August 1994. If this would be a greater majority, I think it would be wiser to use another map, because it then is mainly not relating to the period covered by the indictment. So would you please keep this in mind while questioning the witness on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you also indicate, given that the next break will be longer than the usual break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. I have to apologise, because I had forgotten that I would compensate you for the ten lost minutes. I'd say we'll have a break until ten minutes past 12.00 -- of course, ten minutes past 1.00. I apologise. --- Break taken at 12.37 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're on your feet. I first have to say that I overcompensated you, which is totally against my nature, but well, that's what happens. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I will leave the floor to my colleague. But I wanted to present my apologies to the interpretation booths. Sometimes we use very harsh words because it is very important to bear in mind this exchange, the sequence of questions and answers, because of what we have to deal with afterwards. We have to go back to certain things that were uttered before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one ignores how important the translation is, so that's -- that goes without saying. Please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. With your permission, I should like to remind you that we have to respond to the submissions of my learned colleague in respect of Rule 94 bis as regards the testimony of an expert witness. This morning we have the issue, and I have the obligation to present our position. Whether you want me to do this today or next morning when we finish with the witness, I'm entirely in Your Honour's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it cannot be done at this moment, because we're still waiting for the translations. Because the Chamber, in order to determine whether all the requirements of Article 92 bis are fulfilled, needs to have a look in these statements. I saw that yesterday the same issue came up in the Milosevic case, and we cannot -- I think we'll discuss it while we all have the statements there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Maybe there is a misunderstanding. I'm referring to the Rule 94 bis. If that should be convenient, I should like to state my position tomorrow before we resume with the witness, or today at the end of the day. I only need two minutes to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me -- yes, the expert -- yes, I now better understand. I apologise for not taking proper notice of what you said. Perhaps you could do it tomorrow. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, when in 1995 did the armed conflict cease in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: In 1995, when the conflict ceased, I believe it was towards the end of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean by that around December 1995?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: November, December, thereabouts. I cannot be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Therefore, the armed conflict lasted for some 45 months, is that correct, from April 1992 until December 1995?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you've told us that 80 per cent of your investigations took place in the last 17 months of those 45 months; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes. My investigation, that is how it happened, which doesn't mean that there were not more attacks than that on Sarajevo. I think that there were more attacks leading up to this period, as regards my investigations, because whatever happened in terms of massacres and similar incidents took place in 1994, towards the end of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, given that answer by you, can I ask you this: Over those 45 months, did the attacks against civilians occur at a constant rate or not, that is, over the whole of the 45 months?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the answer given by the witness, no mention was made of civilians. He was referring to the attacks on Sarajevo in general, which means that not every attack was necessarily against civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I did not have interpretation of the words pronounced by the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the General is also complaining of the fact that he does not have the interpretation, and I myself am not receiving interpretation either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a technical problem, as far as I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is over now. Is having now having translation in a language he or she understands? Okay. Then we may continue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're saying the answer given by the witness, no mention was made of civilians. Yes. Would it be possible for you to rephrase your question? I don't know exactly to what answer Mr. Piletta-Zanin is referring, because on a few occasions the witness testified that he investigated cases where civilian casualties occurred. But if you could clarify it by rephrasing your question, please do so, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, you told us that you exclusively investigated sniping and shelling incidents where civilians were casualties, and you have also said that there were attacks which occurred in 1994, towards the end of 1994, which don't necessarily reflect your investigation figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order for me to be able to follow, could Mr. Ierace quote the page and the line of the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you're talking about attacks occurred in 1994 -- let me -- yes, could you please find it. I think it was just before, but it's not on my screen any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm happy to withdraw the question and approach it from auto different angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During that four-month period of the arm conflicted, you were a criminal investigator, you've told us.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you were one of many fellow criminal investigators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Your duties exclusively concerned attacks against civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes. Everything that has been discussed today concerned my work, which had nothing to do with the military. So whatever I have testified about concerns the killings of civilians and the incidents where civilians were victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to civilians being targeted -- I withdraw that. In relation to civilians being casualties as a result of shelling and sniping, from month to month during that 45-month period, was there a constant level of incidents or not?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes. The level of incidents was constant except that we can perhaps single out of year of 1994 as being, at least in my opinion, and from what I heard from my colleagues who also visited scenes of such incidents, was perhaps more intense in terms of incidents than other years.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And was that the whole of 1994 or part of 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: In view of the number of civilian victims, and taking into account massacres such as the one at the Markt Halle, it would be the second half of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there -- when you say the Markt Halle, which particular incident or incidents do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: The one that took place in February 1994, when the massacre at Markt Halle occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that February 1994 is in the first half of 1994 and not the second half, I ask you again whether there were -- whether there was an additional intensity for the whole of 1994 or only part, and if so, which part?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Let me say the following: After the stated period after August 1994, I did many more investigations. However, the number of victims in those incidents was significantly less than the number of victims in the first half of 1994. So the intensity of killings where civilians were victims was greater in this first period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In relation to the investigations that you carried out between September of 1992 and August of 1994, and as a result of other investigations carried out by your fellow criminal inspectors in that same period, were there some sources of sniping fire that repeatedly arose during those investigations as the relevant source?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of my experience, I can tell you about those sources until that part of 1994. We would always gather together, me and my colleagues. We would discuss the cases, we took statements from witnesses, and I can talk about that. There were such sources of fire that were notorious. And I can indicate such locations on an empty map. It doesn't have to be a premarked map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe it's a bit premature to intervene; however, we have had three questions of the same type. The witness spoke about what he has heard from others. I don't know whether one can allow, within the framework of this testimony, that the witness indicates for us on a map, be it a premarked or an empty map, something that he has heard from others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I had intended to clarify that with the next question. Perhaps I could ask that question, and if my friend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then we'll see what still remains of the objection. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to what you heard from others, I ask you to confine yourself to the results of investigations carried out by your fellow criminal inspectors as to the source of fire. Can you do that, please.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In other words, we are confining your sources of information to the results of your own investigations and the investigations of your fellow inspectors.

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You've told us something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you for a clarification, Mr. Ierace. Do you mean by fellow inspectors those inspectors investigating the same cases?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I'll clarify that. I meant others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many investigators were there operating within the city of Sarajevo on the Bosnian government side of the confrontation lines who, like you, investigated cases of civilians becoming casualties as a result of sniping fire and shelling between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: In the town of Sarajevo, there were 20 of us, more or less, from the regional centre for Security Service, plus the inspectors. I mean, those of us who worked on cases involving fatalities. There were other municipal police stations that investigated incidents involving wounding, damage, so there were about 40 additional inspectors, apart from us, who were involved in these types of cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So that's 20 just in investigating cases of fatalities involving civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You've told us something of the techniques that were used in order to establish the source of fire with sniping. To your knowledge, were those techniques used by your fellow inspectors as well?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes. Every investigation team would involve a ballistic expert, and yes, they used the same techniques, every one of the teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you would be able to give the Trial Chamber the positions which recurred during those investigations as sources of sniping fire in that period of September 1992 to August 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Earlier I asked you about a map that you marked, I think last week, with certain positions in relation to the source of sniping fire and shelling fire. Do any of the positions, being the source of sniping fire, in that period, that is, September 1992 to August 1994, appear on that map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but I must object. It is a question which has to do with the map, and the Defence cannot accept it, and we come back to a question which the Chamber has not yet ruled upon. That is, once again, I believe that the Prosecution is placing the cart before the horse, and the Defence cannot accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as far as I can see, there were two issues you raised. The first was the marked map as such, which you withdrew, but that's when you expected that the map would be presented, and the second one is that on this map there would be mainly incidents that occurred in the period after August 1994. Am I correct in my understanding? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if we talk about -- if we take this map, we know what this witness has said, and that is that with regard to incidents that he knows about, that's what he said, 80 per cent had to do with the investigations following the period of the indictment. If it is those incidents which are on this map, then I do not know, because I did not see it, but then the Defence believes that the production of this map and all the questions would represent a biased nature of -- a biased address -- a biased tackling of this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I then instructed Mr. Ierace that he first should find out whether any markings on the map related to these incidents you just mentioned, the 80 per cent. The question of Mr. Ierace was: "Earlier I asked about a map that you marked I think last week with certain positions in relation to the sources of sniping fire and shelling fire. Do any of the positions, being the source of sniping fire, in that period, that is, September 1992 to August 1994, appear on that map?" So I understood the question of Mr. Ierace as to find out what markings, at least markings related to incidents during what period of time would appear on that map. And if we have an answer to that question, then we can then, of course, decide upon the objection you made, that if the map would contain markings related to incidents after August 1994, that we should not admit it into evidence, if I'm correct in my understanding. I would say that, Mr. Ierace, perhaps you may repeat the question to the witness and then stop after we have got an answer from the witness in order to see what next has to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, in relation to the map that you marked last week, in which you indicated certain sources of sniping fire, do any of the sources of sniping fire established by you and your fellow investigators between September 1992 and August 1994 appear on that map?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are there any sniping positions marked on that map which were not active in terms of targeting civilians according to the investigations of yourself and your fellow inspectors, during the period September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: You mean which were activated at a later period? Do you mean whether we discovered some new -- identified some new positions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is if there are any sniping positions on the map, that is, sources of sniping fire, which relate to a different period than between September 1992 and -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just see whether I can assist you, Mr. Ierace? You made some markings on a map, which I have not seen, about sources of sniping fire. Are there markings on the map of sources of sniping fire that became known to you only after August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Those markings are places which I was aware ever since I started conducting those investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So on the basis of your investigations, every single mark on that map relates to a source of sniping fire you identified already during your or your colleagues' investigations prior to or in August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, during this period that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means up until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are there any positions marked as sources of sniping fire on the map which were active only before September 1992 and not between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to the marks that you placed on the map to indicate sources of shelling, in particular, mortars, were all of those positions active sources of such fire between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you base your answer on investigations carried out by yourself and by fellow criminal investigators with the assistance of ballistics experts?

utterances.speaker: Mirsad Kucanin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown the map, which is Exhibit P3658.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with regard to this map, I'm listening attentively to the debate, and I must remind of the Defence's position that we have not been able to cooperate in studying this map, which is very detailed, and it is -- I do not think that it is presenting the factual situation to this Chamber, and I don't that I premarked map and premarked with such a detailed -- in such a detailed manner should be accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I first ask you: In the transcript it reads that you have not been able to cooperate in studying this map. Could you please explain what you exactly meant by "to cooperate in studying this map."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. No. It is obviously a difficulty. I will rephrase what we were saying. In order to respect fully the principle of equality of arms, we need to see how such a map could be made in the process of its making, so that everybody, including the Chamber. By cooperation, I meant to say to see how this map came about, and we have not been able to participate in this process because this map was marked in a unilateral manner, and we were not able to assist, to be present in the process. Thank you. That is all what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hand up a copy of a statement dated the 12th of November, 1995, which was disclosed to the Defence on the 9th of May, 2000. A version in Bosnian was disclosed on the 9th of January, 2001. And I refer you, Mr. President, to three pages, commencing with the number 70 at the end of the ERN reference. Mr. President, you will see there are three pages that set out by street name the positions which have been placed on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Ierace, the objection of Mr. Piletta-Zanin is not perhaps that it is not clear enough, what has been marked and in what detail, but that such detailed maps should only be admitted into evidence if the Defence has been able to attend the marking as such. I think, if I did understand that well, and perhaps after having listened again to Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that this would be a subject to consider until tomorrow morning, but we'd like to hear from Mr. Piletta-Zanin now what additional observation he has to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I am very happy that Mr. Ierace raised this document to explain how this document was done. This document is of the 10th, 11th of November, 1995, and we see that this document, which is the preliminary statement of the witness, it mentions a number of incidents, and I'm giving you the 18th of August 1995, 13th of May, 1995, and then I see here, and so on and so forth, and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this is document 01039343, which I'm reading, and this map was then done on the basis of information related to a period which clearly came after the period which concerns his Excellency, General Galic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having heard the submissions of the parties to the issue, the Chamber would prefer to give its decision on this issue right at the beginning of tomorrow morning. On the other hand, I want to make clear to the parties as well that they should prepare both for the situation where the marked map will be admitted in evidence, but also for the situation that a new map should be used for the continuation of the examining of the witness. So then we'll have a bit more time to consider it, and both parties are ready tomorrow morning at 9.00 to proceed. Let me just make one other remark. Mr. Ierace, may I remind you that you used two hours and 40 minutes, even if I deduct a lot of other issues. And apart from that, I don't know whether the recalling of Mr. Harding would be disturbed by the time we used today and the time we expect to use tomorrow morning. Would you please give this some thought so that we do not have unnecessarily to have witnesses wait for long periods of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the latest I heard was that he was planning on travelling back to The Hague tonight. It may be wise if he has sufficient time to delay that until tomorrow night in order to give evidence on Friday. I'll see if that can be arranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'd just like you to pay attention to it in order to prevent any unnecessary waiting for the witnesses. Mr. Kucanin, we'll have to stop for this day. Tomorrow morning we'll continue at 9.00 in this same courtroom. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of February 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.51 p.m.,
